concepts.name: IUCN Red List Categories: Criteria and Classification
key_dimensions: Distinction between Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), and Vulnerable (VU) — precise thresholds and population decline criteria
UPSC trap: 'Extinct in the Wild' vs 'Locally Extinct' vs 'Extinct' — differences and Indian examples for each
Near Threatened (NT) and Least Concern (LC) — why these are NOT threatened categories but frequently confused as such
Data Deficient (DD) classification — implications for conservation policy and why it is not a threatened category

concepts.name: Wildlife Protection Act 1972: Schedule Classification and Its Link to Threatened Species
key_dimensions: Schedule I vs Schedule II vs Schedule IV — levels of protection and penalties; UPSC trap: Schedule I does NOT equate to IUCN CR status
2022 Amendment: Consolidation of schedules from 6 to 4 — what changed, which schedules were merged
Species in Schedule I that are NOT critically endangered (e.g., Bengal Tiger) vs species that are CR but may have lower schedule listing — mismatches
Vermin category under WPA and its conflict with conservation — historical use against Nilgai, wild boar

concepts.name: Project Tiger: Legal Framework, Coverage, and Critical Tiger Reserves
key_dimensions: Statutory basis: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) under WPA 1972 (Section 38L) — not a standalone act
Buffer zone vs Core zone mandate — no human activity in core; UPSC trap: 'inviolate' applies only to core zones
Tiger Census methodology shift: Camera traps + pug marks to DNA-based + camera trap (2018 census) — implications for data accuracy
Critically Tiger Endangered Landscapes (CTELs) and tiger corridors — which reserves are connected vs isolated (e.g., Sariska, Panna — local extinction and reintroduction)

concepts.name: Project Elephant and Asian Elephant Conservation Status
key_dimensions: Asian Elephant IUCN status: Endangered (EN) — frequently confused with African Elephant (Vulnerable); key distinction for MCQs
Elephant Corridors in India — Elephant Task Force recommendations; 101 identified corridors; legal protection gap
Human-Elephant Conflict (HEC) — fragmentation of corridors, 'problem elephant' declaration under WPA
UPSC trap: Elephants are NOT under Project Tiger; NTCA does NOT manage elephants — Project Elephant is under MoEFCC directly

concepts.name: Critically Endangered Species in India: Key Species Profiles and Habitats
key_dimensions: Must-know CR species: Great Indian Bustard (GIB), Gharial, Hangul (Kashmir Stag), Malabar Large-spotted Civet, Namdapha Flying Squirrel — habitats and states
UPSC trap: Great Indian Bustard is CR (not Endangered); found in Rajasthan primarily (not Gujarat) — geographic precision tested
Gharial vs Mugger Crocodile vs Saltwater Crocodile — conservation status differences (CR vs LC vs LC) and distribution
Hawksbill Sea Turtle (CR) vs Olive Ridley (VU) — both nest in India but different statuses; Gahirmatha vs Ostional comparison

concepts.name: Great Indian Bustard (GIB): Conservation Conflict with Renewable Energy
key_dimensions: Supreme Court order (2021) on underground power cables vs overhead lines in GIB habitat — MoEFCC vs Ministry of Power conflict
GIB habitat overlap with solar energy zones in Rajasthan (Thar Desert) — policy dilemma between SDG 7 and SDG 15
Captive breeding program at Sam, Rajasthan — challenges of low reproductive rate (1 egg per year)
UPSC trap: GIB is State Bird of Rajasthan, NOT Gujarat; also found in Maharashtra, Karnataka in smaller numbers — 'only Rajasthan' is a trap

concepts.name: Marine Threatened Species: Sea Turtles, Dugongs, and Whale Sharks
key_dimensions: Five sea turtle species in India: Olive Ridley (VU), Leatherback (VU), Green (EN), Hawksbill (CR), Loggerhead (VU) — status differences are exam-relevant
Dugong: Vulnerable (IUCN), found only in Gulf of Mannar and Andaman & Nicobar in India — UPSC trap: NOT found in Lakshadweep
Whale Shark: Endangered (IUCN), Schedule I of WPA — only shark under Schedule I; Gujarat fishing community conflict
CCMB's eDNA techniques for marine species monitoring — emerging conservation technology angle

concepts.name: Vulture Crisis in India: Diclofenac, Species Status, and Recovery Programs
key_dimensions: Diclofenac (veterinary NSAID) as primary cause — renal failure in vultures feeding on treated cattle carcasses; banned in 2006 but meloxicam allowed
UPSC trap: Diclofenac ban was for VETERINARY use in 2006; human use was never banned — frequently confused
Species affected: White-rumped Vulture, Indian Vulture, Slender-billed Vulture — all CR; Himalayan Griffon is LC — status distinctions
Vulture Safe Zones (VSZs) and Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre (Pinjore) — ex-situ conservation approach

concepts.name: Snow Leopard Conservation: Project Snow Leopard and Transboundary Challenges
key_dimensions: IUCN status change: Snow Leopard moved from Endangered to Vulnerable in 2017 — UPSC frequently tests outdated vs current status
SECURE Himalaya Project (UNDP-GEF funded) vs Project Snow Leopard (Government) — overlap and distinction in mandate
Range states and transboundary conservation: India, China, Mongolia, Nepal — Global Snow Leopard and Ecosystem Protection (GSLEP) program
Prey base depletion (Blue Sheep/Bharal, Ibex) as primary threat — indirect human pressure angle

concepts.name: Gangetic River Dolphin: National Aquatic Animal and Conservation Status
key_dimensions: Declared National Aquatic Animal in 2009 — UPSC trap: River Dolphin, NOT Irrawaddy Dolphin or Ganges Shark
IUCN status: Endangered; Schedule I of WPA; also found in Brahmaputra (Brahmaputra River Dolphin — same species)
Project Dolphin launched 2020 — modeled on Project Tiger; covers both river and marine dolphins
Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary (Bihar) — only dolphin sanctuary in India; location-based MCQ trap

concepts.name: One-Horned Rhinoceros: Conservation Success Story and Remaining Threats
key_dimensions: IUCN status: Vulnerable (downlisted from Endangered in 2008) — conservation success narrative; population ~4000 globally
96% population in India and Nepal; India: Kaziranga (>2600), Pobitora (highest density globally), Orang, Manas
UPSC trap: Rhino is NOT only in Assam — also in West Bengal (Jaldapara, Gorumara); 'only Kaziranga' is incorrect
Rhino horn poaching and linkage to Chinese traditional medicine market — transnational wildlife crime angle

concepts.name: Lion-Tailed Macaque and Western Ghats Endemic Threatened Species
key_dimensions: Lion-Tailed Macaque: Endangered (IUCN), endemic to Western Ghats — found in Silent Valley, Anamalai Hills; NOT Himalayan
Western Ghats as a Biodiversity Hotspot — 4 of 36 global hotspots in India; Gadgil Committee vs Kasturirangan Committee on ESA classification
Nilgiri Tahr (Endangered) vs Nilgiri Langur (Vulnerable) — both Western Ghats endemics with different statuses; confusion trap
UPSC trap: Western Ghats hotspot extends across 6 states — Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Gujarat (partial); 'only 4 states' is a common error

concepts.name: Fishing Cat and Wetland-Dependent Threatened Species
key_dimensions: Fishing Cat: Vulnerable (IUCN), Schedule I WPA — associated with mangroves and wetlands; found in Sundarbans, Chilika, Coringa
UPSC trap: Fishing Cat is NOT a fish; it is a wild cat species — taxonomic confusion tested
Irrawaddy Dolphin: Vulnerable, found in Chilika Lake — only inland population in India; distinct from Gangetic Dolphin
Wetland destruction and RAMSAR site protection as conservation tool — linkage between wetland policy and species survival

concepts.name: CITES and India's Obligations: Appendix Classification of Indian Species
key_dimensions: Appendix I vs II vs III — Appendix I: commercial trade prohibited (Tiger, Elephant, Rhino); Appendix II: regulated trade; Appendix III: unilateral listing
UPSC trap: India listed Rosewood (Dalbergia sissoo) under CITES Appendix II in 2017 — plants, not just animals, are covered
Tokay Gecko and Star Tortoise — lesser-known species under CITES; frequently smuggled from India
Conflict between CITES Appendix II listing of Indian Elephant and African Elephant ivory trade proposals — India's consistent opposition at CoP

concepts.name: Invasive Alien Species and Their Impact on Native Threatened Species
key_dimensions: Lantana camara, Prosopis juliflora, Parthenium — top three invasive plants in India impacting native species habitat
UPSC trap: Invasive species are NOT always introduced by humans — some spread naturally; but policy focus is on anthropogenic introductions
Common Myna and Rose-ringed Parakeet impact on native cavity-nesting birds — competition for nesting sites
Biological invasion as the second largest cause of biodiversity loss globally (after habitat destruction) — CBD Article 8(h) obligations

concepts.name: Ex-situ Conservation Institutions and Their Role in Threatened Species Recovery
key_dimensions: Central Zoo Authority (CZA) under WPA 1972 — regulates zoos; UPSC trap: CZA is statutory body under WPA, NOT under a separate Zoo Act
National Gene Bank at NBPGR (New Delhi) — for plant genetic resources; distinct from animal germplasm banks
Frozen Zoo concept and cryopreservation — CCMB's role in preserving genetic material of endangered species
UPSC trap: Ex-situ conservation is NOT preferred over in-situ under CBD; in-situ is primary, ex-situ is supplementary — hierarchy matters

concepts.name: Biosphere Reserves in India: UNESCO MAB Program and Threatened Species Linkage
key_dimensions: 18 Biosphere Reserves in India; 12 in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR) — UPSC trap: NOT all 18 are UNESCO-recognized
Core zone = No human activity; Buffer zone = Limited research; Transition zone = Human settlements allowed — three-zone model precision
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve — Gene sanctuary for wild relatives of citrus; Agasthyamalai — endemic species hotspot in Western Ghats
Difference between Biosphere Reserve, National Park, and Wildlife Sanctuary — overlapping geographies (e.g., Nilgiri BR contains Mudumalai NP)

concepts.name: Amphibian Crisis in India: Purple Frog, Caecilians, and Declining Populations
key_dimensions: Purple Frog (Nasikabatrachus sahyadrensis): Endangered, endemic to Western Ghats — discovered in 2003; 'living fossil' as it is the sole surviving member of ancient family Nasikabatrachidae
India among top 5 countries for amphibian diversity AND amphibian extinction risk — chytrid fungus (Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis) as global threat
UPSC trap: Caecilians are legless amphibians, NOT reptiles — taxonomic confusion; Ichthyophis (caecilian) found in Northeast India
Amphibians as bioindicators — permeable skin makes them sensitive to pollution; policy relevance for wetland conservation

concepts.name: Human-Wildlife Conflict: Policy Framework and Species-Specific Challenges
key_dimensions: National Wildlife Action Plan (2017–2031) — addresses HWC as a priority; compensation schemes under State Wildlife Boards
UPSC trap: Compensation for wildlife attack is a STATE subject under WPA — no uniform national compensation scheme exists
Leopard conflict in peri-urban areas (Mumbai, Uttarakhand) — Leopard is Vulnerable (IUCN) but highest human-wildlife conflict animal in India
Crop-raiding by elephants and wild boar — 'vermin' declaration under Section 62 of WPA; constitutional issue of states declaring Schedule I species as vermin

concepts.name: Species Recovery Programs under MoEFCC: Beyond Tiger and Elephant
key_dimensions: Recovery programs for 22 critically endangered species in India — includes GIB, Dugong, Gangetic Dolphin, Manipur Brow-antlered Deer (Sangai), Jerdon's Courser
Sangai (Manipur Brow-antlered Deer): Endangered, found ONLY in Keibul Lamjao National Park — world's only floating national park; 'phumdis' habitat
UPSC trap: Keibul Lamjao is a National Park, NOT a Wildlife Sanctuary — its floating nature makes it unique but its legal status is NP
Hirola (Hunter's Hartebeest) — NOT an Indian species; UPSC sometimes mixes African CR species with Indian ones in options
